call_points.text: FY27 revenue guided at ₹5,500 Cr with about 13% EBITDA margin; Q1 is in line with that.
Core business volume guidance held at 105-110 million meters and core revenue at about ₹4,000 Cr.
New business (utility bedding plus US brands) kept at a ₹1,500 Cr FY27 revenue target.
Long-term target is to stabilise at 15-16% margins for the company as a whole.
US manufacturing utilisation held at 60-65% despite the new North Carolina greenfield plant added in January 2026.
Utility bedding utilisation is targeted at 60-65% for the full year, stable at Q1 levels.
Bed linen and utility bedding are both expected to do 15% margins; the brand business 100-200 bps better.
Management aspires to ₹8,000 Cr revenue by CY2028, with a USD 275 million new business ambition.
FY27 revenue targeted at ~₹5,500 Cr, over 30% growth.
FY27 volumes guided at 105-110 million meters.
New business revenues for FY26 stood at INR792 crores, supported by consistent sequential growth throughout the year.
Non-US core business was ~30% of core revenue in FY26 and is expected to grow 20% in FY27.
All input costs, including cotton, yarn, gas and packaging, have risen; management expects to pass them on within a quarter.
Final dividend of ₹1.50 per equity share recommended, subject to shareholders' approval.
Management declined to quantify the raw material cost impact or comment on Q1 FY27 margins.
Total capex planned for FY27 is ₹250 Cr, including ETP, maintenance, and brownfield spinning expansion.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Income Tax Department had initially raised a demand aggregating to ₹118.95 crore for the block assessment period covering six assessment years (AY 2012–13 to AY 2017–18). Subsequently, the Department rectified the demand to ₹56.22 crore, against which the Company filed an appeal. Pursuant to the appellate order dated 24.05.2024, the contingent liability in respect of the said demand was reduced to ₹0.17 crore. Further, following the order of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal dated 30.10.2025, the contingent liability now stands at Nil.
tax_litigation.status: The departmental appeals filed against the orders of the CIT(A) were disposed of in favour of the Company vide order dated 30.10.2025.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The GST Department had raised a demand aggregating to ₹3.44 crore (excluding interest and penalty) for the period April 2019 to December 2019, in respect of: (1) services provided to distinct persons, (2) commission on corporate bank guarantees, (3) commission paid to foreign persons on exports, and (4) reverse charge mechanism (RCM) on foreign bank charges. For the said nine-months period, the Company filed individual appeals for each month. Out of these, orders have been received for five appeals pertaining to the months of April to July and November, vide Orders of the Commissioner (Appeals) dated 29.12.2025, 30.12.2025, 05.01.2026, 30.12.2025, and 30.10.2025, respectively. Pursuant to these orders, the demand amounting to ₹2.10 crore out of the total demand of ₹3.44 crore has been substantially reduced to ₹0.09 crore. The Company is in process to file a further appeal before CESTAT against the balance demand within the prescribed timelines.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Maharashtra Goods & Service Tax Department, Kolhapur
tax_litigation.status: The Company is in the process of filing appeals before CESTAT within the prescribed timelines against the said orders.

industry: Consumer Discretionary > Textiles > Textiles & Apparels > Other Textile Products

operating_notes.text: FY26 employee benefits expense includes ₹9.61 Cr one-time past service cost from the four Labour Codes notified on 21 November 2025 (gratuity ₹8.82 Cr, compensated absences ₹0.79 Cr).
Finance cost for FY26 includes ₹12.82 Cr interest paid on delayed IGST refund to Maharashtra State GST authorities following their March 2026 search and inspection of records.
Managerial remuneration of ₹2.96 Cr was paid/provided beyond Section 197 limits; shareholder approval by special resolution is proposed at the ensuing AGM.
New businesses scaled to ₹792 Cr in FY26, representing 19% of total revenue.
New businesses revenue scaled to USD 90 million in FY26, representing 19% of total revenue.
Indo Count approved a ₹60 Cr brownfield expansion at Alte, Kolhapur, increasing spinning capacity from 70,000 to 94,000 spindles with 98% existing capacity utilization.
FY26 new business revenue was ₹792 Cr, of which about two-thirds came from utility bedding and one-third from brands.
US utility bedding facilities are operating at around 65% utilisation, with 60-65% targeted across all three facilities in FY27.
Around 30% of cotton is imported (Egyptian and American long-staple), with 70% sourced domestically.
Q1FY27 core business revenue was ₹837 Cr (up 4% QoQ) and new business revenue ₹387 Cr, with the new business split two-thirds utility bedding and one-third brands.
US manufacturing utilisation was 60-65% in Q1FY27 despite the North Carolina greenfield plant added in January 2026; utility bedding is targeted at 60-65% utilisation for FY27.
About 70% of core business revenue comes from the US and 30% from non-US markets; the UK is 8-10% of business and FTAs are expected to take 12-18 months to pan out.

Orbis Consulting AG as trustee of The Lhochhar Trust indirectly acquired voting rights of Indo Count Industries promoter Sandridge Investments via testamentary transmission.

watchlist.text: Special resolution for managerial remuneration of ₹296.43 lakhs at ensuing AGM
Shareholders' approval for final dividend of ₹1.50 per equity share

watchlist.response: Management declined to give a specific number, saying all input costs have risen and contracts are being repriced.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the specific impact of rising raw material costs on operating performance.

watchlist.response: Management said it is very difficult to comment at this point.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked whether Q4 FY27 exit margin would be above 13%.

watchlist.response: Management declined to comment on a quarterly basis.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked whether Q1 FY27 would be better than Q4 FY26.

watchlist.response: Declined to guide at that precision; said the endeavour is to maintain a 13% blended consolidated margin for the full year.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked whether Q2/Q3 standalone margins would fall given Bhilad disruption and higher costs.

watchlist.response: Management said there can be ups and downs and that 60-65% is a satisfactory level, without giving a ramp path.
watchlist.text: Analyst pressed on why utility bedding utilisation would stay at 60-65% for the year when Q1 was already near that level.

watchlist.response: Said no material benefit is expected, about 80% of exports are FOB, and it would be premature to quantify; clarity expected by year-end.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the size of any US tariff refund benefit.
